entries.test: Public financing, investment and business-failure data would show whether the AI boom ends when data-center debt and startup venture funding become unavailable.
entries.note: The surrounding text gives the funding condition a concrete financial meaning.
Economics that 'don't really make sense' has no shared financial threshold.
The assertion concerns entire investor classes' private willingness to invest, rather than just their recorded investments.

entries.test: OpenAI's reported quarterly compute expenditure would establish whether $11 billion covers a quarter at its current spending rate.
entries.note: This is a comparison with current quarterly costs, despite the word 'won't'.
The proposition drops 'If OpenAI needed' and retains only the probabilistic explanation.
The central assertion evaluates the fundraising outcome as extremely bad. The amounts and valuations could be checked separately.

entries.test: OpenAI's investment terms and IPO return arithmetic, alongside contemporaneous Anthropic valuation estimates, would test the claimed valuation requirement and decline.
entries.note: The proposition replaces 'anything close to a positive return' with a positive return and turns two illustrative valuations into a range.
Realizing it should raise as much as possible is not an assertion that it actually raised the maximum possible.

entries.test: Comparable financial disclosures would establish the companies' growth, revenue and costs and OpenAI's free-user advertising revenue relative to serving costs.
entries.note: The listed metrics supply concrete meaning to 'objectively worse'.

entries.test: Public revenue results and reporting on Gulf investors' participation and assessment of GPT-6 Astra would test the claimed failure to stimulate investment.
entries.note: In context, investor excitement means willingness to participate in the funding round.

entries.test: Public fundraising results and investor assessments following GPT-6 Astra would show whether it improved investor reception despite OpenAI's financial fundamentals.
entries.note: The claimed failure is asserted firmly; 'I believe' principally qualifies the model's expected role.
Neither the dimension nor the extent of 'worse' is specified enough to resolve conflicting financial developments.

entries.test: OpenAI's liquidity disclosures and fundraising terms over the months following November 2026 would test its need for new capital and the stated valuation influences.
entries.note: The forecast is emphatic and its near-term horizon has not elapsed.

entries.test: Anthropic's eventual issuer rating and pension-fund and insurer investment restrictions would test the predicted rating and exclusion from major bond buyers.
entries.note: The proposition removes 'essentially' and broadens a claim about the most prolific buyers into an unqualified exclusion.
The rating remains anticipated in the surrounding text. A 'psychological cold shower' supplies no agreed test.

entries.test: Comparative financial statements and public reporting on OpenAI's financing alternatives would test its higher costs, lower revenue and restricted funding options.
entries.note: The source says 'few options outside' these rounds, not 'only options'.
Filing dates establish omission and timing, but the claim additionally asserts a deliberate internal decision to withhold ready numbers.

entries.test: Anthropic's quarterly revenue and usage data, together with customer token-spending policies and budgets, would test whether unrestricted employee usage caused the Q2 anomaly.
entries.note: This is an empirical explanation of a reported quarter.
The claim ties IPO timing to a private intention to precede investor scrutiny. Token-spending cutbacks can be checked separately.
The asserted purpose of misleading investors is a private motive.

entries.test: Anthropic's Q2 and Q3 2026 revenue and compute-cost disclosures would establish the respective percentage increases.
entries.note: The arithmetic is directly testable.

entries.test: Comparable workload, compute-efficiency and pricing disclosures would establish whether technical efficiency accounts for the reported cost gap.
entries.note: The source expresses disbelief in an explanation; the proposition turns that skepticism into a categorical denial.
Explicitly presented as a guess and qualified by 'likely'.
The source says it 'almost feels like' intentional misleading; 'seems meant' strengthens that tentative suspicion.

entries.test: Anthropic's contractual-obligation disclosures and financial results would test the commitment totals, non-cancellable amount and claimed failure to achieve sustainable economics.
entries.note: The insult does not erase the concrete financial assertions.

entries.test: Anthropic's filing would show whether the additional arrangements total roughly $300 billion and how they are presented relative to the obligations table.
entries.note: The amount and disclosure structure are checkable; 'deceptive' also adds an evaluative characterization.
This alleges an intention to deceive retail investors.

entries.test: Anthropic's successive cash-flow statements would show whether its cash burn reaches billions of dollars and increases over time.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supports reading the awkward 'increasing intervals' as increasing cash burn.

entries.test: Anthropic's payment disclosures through late 2030 would show the compute costs incurred and the size and timing of upfront payments.
entries.note: The four-year horizon remains in the future.

entries.test: Anthropic's upcoming cash-flow and contract disclosures would establish significant prepayments and $9.3 billion quarterly SpaceX spending if the agreement does not expand.
entries.note: The proposition drops the explicit agreement-size condition and softens the exact quarterly amount to 'about'.

entries.test: Successive annual expense disclosures would test whether Anthropic's costs rise substantially every year, with a flat or declining year contradicting the claim.
entries.note: The absence of an end date does not make the annual prediction uncheckable.

entries.test: Anthropic's financial results during a compute-spending shortfall relative to revenue would show whether the resulting loss amounts to billions of dollars.
entries.note: In context, 'mismatch' means spending outpacing revenue, not revenue exceeding spending.

entries.test: Anthropic's future debt issuance terms would establish whether it must borrow at interest rates between 8% and 11%.
entries.note: 'All but certain' conveys high confidence rather than a mere possibility.

entries.test: Anthropic's obligation schedule, liquidity, revenue and margins would test whether meeting its commitments requires roughly doubled revenue by November 2027 and continued growth.
entries.note: This asserts a current financial requirement rather than predicting that doubling will occur. In context, size refers to revenue.

entries.test: Customer revenue composition and customer funding data would establish the approximately 80% share and the extent of growth's dependence on venture financing.
entries.note: The proposition drops 'mostly' from the asserted dependence and omits the customers' heavy subsidies.
The source conditionally estimates a $50 billion need; the proposition treats that need as established. Difficulty seeing a path is expressed as uncertainty.
It asserts Anthropic's private realization. The proposition also narrows 'everybody' to 'people'.
'Unclear how' expresses uncertainty about survival mechanisms; 'doubtful that' strengthens it into an adverse probability judgment.

entries.test: Contemporaneous financing outcomes, bond-market access and investor commentary would show whether backlogs and growth projections were still attracting investment.
entries.note: The surrounding financing discussion supplies a concrete reading of 'impress'.

entries.test: Coverage in major news outlets and mainstream financial research would establish whether concerns about neocloud viability had become widespread.
entries.note: The source explicitly anchors 'mainstream' in major-media coverage.

entries.test: Market movements and contemporaneous analyst and investor reactions following the earnings releases would test whether those results caused widespread financial alarm.
entries.note: The sentence attributes the market reaction to earnings.

entries.test: Amazon's and Google's earnings releases, consensus forecasts and segment disclosures would establish the double misses and sources of cloud growth.
entries.note: The proposition weakens 'double-misses' to an unspecified earnings miss.

entries.test: Google's search-monetization disclosures and cloud revenue exposure to OpenAI and Anthropic would test the asserted effects of AI investment.
entries.note: The proposition removes 'appeared' and shifts the specific monetization cause from AI Overviews to AI spending generally.

entries.test: Microsoft's OpenAI-related revenue disclosures and contemporaneous reporting on OpenAI fundraising would establish increasing revenue concentration alongside funding difficulties.
entries.note: 'Alarmingly' is evaluative, but the underlying financial trend is concrete.

entries.test: Azure's quarter-over-quarter revenue breakdown and OpenAI compute payments would establish whether increased OpenAI spending accounts for the $3.8 billion growth.
entries.note: The attribution is emphatic, notwithstanding the following paragraph's conditional wording.
Calling results mediocre relative to unspecified promises is an assessment of worth without an agreed performance standard.

entries.test: Subscription prices, included token value, serving costs and subsequent price or usage-limit changes across AI services would test widespread subsidies and later retrenchment.
entries.note: 'Most' weakens 'the vast majority'. The passage describes a business pattern already occurring.

entries.test: Replit's subscription revenue, service-delivery costs and gross margins would establish whether it sold services below cost.
entries.note: The proposition captures Zitron's explicit rejection of Masad's claim, supported by the following discussion.
This is a sweeping polemical characterization, not a specified allegation of fraud.

entries.test: Future pricing and usage-policy changes would show whether subsidized AI subscriptions lose included usage or become materially more expensive.
entries.note: Zitron explicitly adopts the prediction in his own voice and with full confidence.
'Suggesting' presents a tentative inference. December dates the usage-policy change, not a firm deadline for subsidies to end.
'I imagine' makes this a speculative extension across the industry.

entries.test: Public funding, valuation, investment and failure data would show whether the AI boom collapses when its financing dries up.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraphs define the money as venture funding and infrastructure debt.

entries.test: If venture funding ends before public-market access, company filings and default or restructuring records would show whether OpenAI and Anthropic cannot meet their commitments.
entries.note: 'Crushed' has a plain financial reading in this context.

entries.test: Customer funding and revenue disclosures would test the dependence on venture subsidies and whether those subsidies eventually cease.
entries.note: The eventual exhaustion of subsidies is asserted firmly without a deadline.

entries.test: Data-center financing disclosures and subsequent NVIDIA growth and construction data would test whether debt dominates funding and whether its withdrawal slows both outcomes.
entries.note: The current financing premise is separately checkable now.

entries.test: If Anthropic seeks debt during a data-center credit pullback, public loan terms and financing outcomes would show whether borrowing becomes costlier or less available.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion makes 'harder' refer to financing its obligations.

entries.test: Subsequent fundraising outcomes, subscription restrictions, neocloud debt access and Anthropic valuations would show whether the listed financial pressures intensify.
entries.note: The listed indicators give concrete content to the figurative prediction.
